2. Facts briefly stated are that the present pre-emptor-opposite party Nos. 1-6 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1998 in the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Begurngonj, Noakhali under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act praying for pre-emption of the case land alleging, infer alia, that they are co-sharer tenants in the case jote by way of inheritance as well as by purchase and their co-sharer pre-emptee opposite party No.3, Rafique Ullah sold 24 decimals of land to pre-emptee opposite party Nos. 1-2 by a registered sale deed No. 11986 dated 21-12-1997 who are strangers to the case jote. No notice of the said transfer was served upon the preemptors as a co-sharer and having learnt about the said transfer they took out certified copy of the said deed of transfer on 2-1-1998 and thereafter filed the case within 4(four) months from date of the said transfer and prayed for pre-emption to the case land. 

 8. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the Judgment of the Courts below including the evidence and other materials on record. It appears that 2 courts below upon assigning reasons concurrently found that the pre-emptor opposite parties proved their right as co-sharer tenants. It also appears from the judgment of the Courts below that both the Courts below taking into consideration the documentary evidence along with oral evidence adduced by the parties arrived at a positive finding that with a view to defeating the right of the preemption of the present pre-emptor-opposite parties, the seller (pre-emptee No.3) and the purchasers (pre-emptee Nos. 1-2) collusively made the said transfer as a mortgage although in reality the said transfer is an out and out sale. Furthermore, it appears from the observation of the trial Court that on 18-2-2001 the contesting pre-emptee-opposite-parties by filing an application stated that all necessary parties having been impleaded and accordingly, the case does not suffer for defect of parties. 

 11. The proposition of law under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is very clear that to shut the door against all the strangers who shall encroach upon the ownership and possession of the real co-sharers and whereupon the real co-sharers can remain in enjoyment of their property and others cannot interfere with their right and possession. So, I find substance and force in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the pre-emptor-opposite parties that the pre-ernptees in collusion with each other by way of practicing fraud upon the Court obtained a fraudulent soleh decree in Title Suit No. 30 of 1998 in order to defeat the pre-emptor's right of pre-emption and the said fraudulent soleh decree cannot be allowed to stand in the way of pre-emption, which is otherwise available to the pre-ernptors.
